# Promoted to repo memory: rust-core

which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-09-21T10:12:52.839Z) — A vitest run that hangs in CI with no failure (job cancelled at the 6h limit) is a file that never finished: vitest prints a file's results only on completion, so diff the files the CI log reported against `git ls-files '*.test.ts'`. Never point a test's "unwritable" path under /proc: on Linux, mkdirSync({recursive:true}) there loops forever (ENOENT/EEXIST retry), a sync spin no test timeout can interrupt; use a path under a regular file (ENOTDIR on every platform, even as root). Reproduce Linux-only behaviour locally with Docker (`open -a Docker`, then node:20 / node:24 images).
- **M2** (2026-09-21T16:23:11.699Z) — sofar_update_plan (plan_updated) rebuilds the phase objects, so every phase NOTE set by an earlier phase_status_changed is silently dropped. The fold warns only about task and phase STATUSES, and the plan schema has no field to restate a note. After any plan replacement, re-issue sofar_update_phase with the same status and note for each phase that had one. To write to a record that lives on another worktree's branch (e.g. rust-core in ~/IO/sofar-rust-core) from a session whose MCP server is bound to main, spawn `sofar mcp` with cwd set to that worktree and call the tools over stdio JSON-RPC (initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/call). A plan_updated from main's stale copy would clobber the branch plan on union. Event-only writes (notes, memories, session events) can instead go through main and be carried over with `sofar export <slug>` | `sofar import - <slug> --root <worktree>`, which dedupes by id.
- **M3** (2026-09-22T07:28:34.294Z) — Run long perf harnesses on this laptop under `caffeinate -ims` (e.g. `caffeinate -ims npx vitest run --project perf`). If the Mac idle-sleeps mid-run, especially on battery overnight, the harness fails with `spawnSync ... ETIMEDOUT` at a random measure or inside prepare(). The 120 s spawn timeout counts wall-clock time, and that includes the sleep. The same spawns run directly take 1-4 s. Diagnose with `pmset -g log | grep -E 'Entering Sleep|DarkWake'` over the run's window. Found 2026-09-22 when two team100 A/B runs died this way (sleep at 23:56 and 23:58 for 1,050 s).
